summary: Mayumi Nasu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She held a lecturer post at Shuchiin University (attested 2011–2013) and was a specially appointed associate professor at Koyasan University (attested 2026).

Małgorzata Sulich-Cowley works in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. She studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University, the University of Lausanne, and the University of Warsaw (PhD 2013), later working at SWPS University (2015) and the University of Warsaw (2018–2021).

McComas Taylor, an Indologist, earned his PhD from the Australian National University. His career includes leadership and faculty roles at ANU (from 2005), Banaras Hindu University (attested 2008), the University of Michigan (attested 2016), and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies (attested 2025).

McKim Marriott (1924–2024) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Harvard under Clyde Kluckhohn and completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~1946–1955). He served as professor of anthropology and social sciences at Chicago from ~1955 to 1998.

Md Mohiuddin Ahmed Tanvir, who works in Buddhist and religious studies, earned a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Dhaka (2019–2023). He subsequently served as a counsellor at AHZ Bangladesh (2024–2025), IDP Education (2025–2026), and Kampus Group (2026).

Medawachchiye Dhammajothi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and Nanjing University (PhD ~2005). In 2008, he held lectureships at Colombo, PBIPS, and BPU.
Medhani is a scholar who studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Megan Bryson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (2002–2010) and served as an associate professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (attested 2017).

Megumu Honda (1931–2011) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Johannes Rahder (1961–1962), Paul Tedesco, and Rulon Wells. He served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).

Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger and Dieter Schuh, and was attested as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies in 2026.
Meiji Yamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku University (attested 1962), he also served as a professor there (attested 1963–1971 and 2007).

Meinrad Scheller (1921–1991), a linguist and Indologist, studied at Charles University, Paris, and Zurich under Manu Leumann, Julius Pokorny, and Ernst Risch. He held posts at Thesaurus Linguae Latinae, Fribourg, Munich, and the University of Zurich (1956; 1975–1988).
Meiping Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).
Melissa R. Kerin is a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who completed her doctoral studies under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter.

Melvyn C. Goldstein is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his BA from the University of Michigan (~1955–1959) and his PhD from the University of Washington (~1960–1968). He served as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Mengqiu Tian is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned a master's degree from Heidelberg University (2019–2022) and became an FWO PhD research fellow and doctoral researcher at Ghent University (2025–2026).

Merab Mamardashvili (1930–1990) was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held academic posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Meredith Borthwick (1950–1995) was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Melbourne (BA, MA ~1968–1975) and the Australian National University (PhD ~1976–1980). She became a head at the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade in 1980.

Mervin Viggo Hanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz and also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.

Mervyn Sprung (1913–2000) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Manitoba, the University of Toronto, and Humboldt University of Berlin (PhD ~1936–1939), and served as professor of philosophy at Brock University (1965–1979).
